text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-President Hrawi will start consultations with the MPs today and tomorrow to nominate a new prime minister.
-Nabih Berri remained speaker of the parliament after he was re-elected in the first session of the new parliament.
-Lebanon's trade deficit is more than $4.7 billion in the first nine months of 1996.
-School teachers will go on a one-day strike on November 14 to press pay demands and will begin an open-ended strike on December 4 if their demands are not met.
-Israeli helicopters strafe areas in southeastern Lebanon north of the eastern sector of Israel's south Lebanon zone before midnight.

-Berri, in a speech to parliament after his re-election, stresses the need to close the file of the tens of thousands of families displaced by the civil war and the necessity of a just parliamentary elections law.
-Beirut port revenue rose 40 percent in the first nine months of this year.
-President Hrawi held lengthy talks with Syrian President Assad in Damascus on Tuesday on regional and internal issues.
-The committee grouping audovisual media workers demanded that the government give their institutions extra time to lodge applications to get licences.
